subject: How can i call gird.arrange  with a variable number of graphics  objects

messages.author: ff42271ef6191bca
messages.subject: How can i call gird.arrange  with a variable number of graphics  objects
parts:
I am trying to dynamically build an arrangement of graphs using
grid.arrange, but can't figure out how to call grid.arrange() with a
variable number of grobs.

The total number of objects and rows depends on some parameters, so i
would like to have a single function call but dynamically provide
"nrow=1" and "p1, p2" or "nrow=2" with "p1, p2, p3" as required.

Is there a simple way?

Thanks,
Herbert

--simple example--------------------------------------
require(ggplot2)
require(ggExtra)

x <- rnorm(100)
y <- rnorm(100)
z <- rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(x=x, y=y, z=z)

p1 <- ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(x, y)) +
scale_x_continuous(name='') +
scale_y_continuous(name='')
p2 <- ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(y, x)) +
scale_x_continuous(name='') +
scale_y_continuous(name='')
p3 <- ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(y, z)) +
scale_x_continuous(name='') +
scale_y_continuous(name='')

numgraphs <- 3

dev.new(width=6, height=6)
grid.newpage()
if (numgraphs == 2) {
grid.arrange(nrow=1,
p1, p2,
sub=textGrob(expression('Time (ms)'),
gp=gpar(font=1)),
left=textGrob(expression('Amplitude (' * mu * 'V)'),
gp=gpar(font=1), rot=90))
}
if (numgraphs == 3) {
grid.arrange(nrow=2,
p1, p2, p3,
sub=textGrob(expression('Time (ms)'),
gp=gpar(font=1)),
left=textGrob(expression('Amplitude (' * mu * 'V)'),
gp=gpar(font=1), rot=90))
}

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: How can i call gird.arrange with a variable number of graphics  objects
parts:
Hi,


I think you want to use do.call with a list of arguments,

do.call(grid.arrange, list(p1,p2,p3, ncol=1, sub="some text",
left="other text"))


HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: RE: How can i call gird.arrange with a variable number of graphics 	objects
parts:
Hi Herbert and Baptiste,

Based on your codes, I think could arrange a more general function.

Hope this helps,
fernnado

PS. I used gridExtra instead of ggExtra


require(ggplot2)
require(gridExtra)

k <- rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(x=x, y=y, z=z, k = k)


myfunc <- function(df, nr)
{
require(ggplot2)
require(gridExtra)
require(gregmisc)
vnames <- names(df)
comb <- combinations(n = length(vnames), r = 2, vnames)
k <- dim(comb)[1]
mplots <- vector("list", k + 3)
for (i in 1:k)
{
mplots[[i]] <- ggplot(df) +
geom_point(aes_string(x = comb[i, 1], y = comb[i,
2])) +

names(mplots)[i] <- paste("p", i, sep = "")
}
names(mplots)[ (k + 1) : (k + 3) ] <- c("nrow", "sub", "left")
mplots[[k + 1]] <- nr
mplots[[k + 2]] <- textGrob(expression('Time (ms)'),
gp=gpar(font=1))
mplots[[k + 3]] <- textGrob(expression('Amplitude (' * mu * 'V)'),
gp=gpar(font=1), rot=90)

dev.new(width=6, height=6)
grid.newpage()
do.call(arrange, mplots)
}

myfunc(df, 2)
